title: The Ass in the Tiger-Skin

full_text:
In a manufacturing town lived an impoverished, lazy washerman named Sthirabuddhi. He owned an old, half-starved domestic donkey who was so weak from hunger that he could scarcely stumble under the weight of the laundry baskets.

One afternoon, while walking through the forest, the washerman found the carcass of a magnificent, striped royal Bengal tiger that had been slain by a hunter and stripped of its meat. The hunter had left the skin drying upon the bushes.

The cunning washerman thought: 'What a miraculous prize! I will take this tiger skin, wrap it securely around my starving donkey, and turn him loose by night into the rich barley and wheat fields of the neighboring farmers! Mistaking him for a ferocious tiger, the watchmen will flee in terror, and my beast can gorge himself on ripe grain until he is fat and strong!'

The washerman draped the heavy tiger skin over the donkey, securing the head and tail with leather thongs. That evening, he drove the disguised beast into a farmer's lush field of ripe green barley.

Seeing a colossal, striped 'tiger' standing in the moonlight munching grain, the terrified field watchmen dropped their lanterns, abandoned their watchtowers, and fled to the village, shouting: 'A monstrous royal tiger has invaded the fields!'

Night after night, the donkey feasted in comfort, growing sleek, fat, and muscular, while the terrified farmers dared not venture near their crops.

One moonlit midnight, as the donkey stood grazing contentedly in the barley, a stray female donkey tied to a cart on a distant lane caught the scent of the night breeze and brayed with a high, clear note: 'Hee-haw! Hee-haw!'

Hearing the romantic call of his own species, the disguised donkey felt an uncontrollable thrill of excitement. His ancestral blood surged; his long ears twitched beneath the tiger skin, and forgetting his disguise, his danger, and his master's warnings, he threw back his head and brayed with all his might: 'HEE-HAW! HEE-HAW! HEE-HAW!'

The sound echoed across the silent fields.

The farmers, huddled behind the village stockade armed with clubs and arrows, froze in amazement: 'Listen! That is no tiger roaring! That is the braying of an ordinary washerman's donkey wrapped in a tiger's skin!'

Enraged at having been made fools of by a common ass, the farmers rushed into the field armed with heavy iron-tipped staves, sticks, and slings. Surrounding the braying imposter, they beat him so mercilessly that the foolish donkey perished upon the barley field he had plundered.

Thus Vishnu Sharma taught:
"The borrowed skin of majesty may shield an empty head,
And fill the simple multitude with trembling fear and dread;
Yet let the boaster speak one word, his secret is betrayed,
And justice beats the braying fool beneath the open glade."
moral: An imposter may prosper as long as he remains silent; but the moment he opens his mouth, his folly is revealed.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Ass in the Tiger-Skin"?
options: Wisdom, honesty, and kindness guide the heart toward lasting peace.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
